questions.q: What does the Application Repository actually track?
options: A list of every Incident ever created in an instance
Only the names of users who have logged into an instance
Published versions of a scoped application as a coherent whole
Individual field-level dictionary changes only
questions.explain: The Application Repository is a central store for tracking numbered, published versions of an entire scoped application.

questions.q: What does each published version in the Application Repository capture?
options: Only the Update Sets that happened to be active that day
Nothing; versions are just labels with no actual content
A single isolated script with nothing else included
The entire application — its tables, fields, scripts, and UI elements — at that point in time
questions.explain: A published version is a complete, numbered snapshot of the whole application, not a partial record.

questions.q: Why does reasoning about "the old version of the app" get hard with Update Sets alone?
options: Because Update Sets can only be created by administrators, never developers
Because there's no single stored answer for which sequence of Update Sets, in which order, represents a past state — it has to be reconstructed from history
It never gets hard; Update Sets always make this trivial
Because Update Sets delete themselves automatically after a week
questions.explain: Update Sets capture individual changes; figuring out which combination represents a past application state takes reconstruction, not a lookup.

questions.q: What does rolling back using the Application Repository actually involve?
options: Manually rewriting every Business Rule by hand from memory
Reversing an unknown number of individual Update Sets in the correct order
Deleting the entire scoped application and starting over
Pulling a specific prior published version — one coherent, already-validated snapshot — back onto the instance
questions.explain: A version rollback treats the whole application as one unit, which is exactly what makes it simpler and safer than reversing individual changes.

questions.q: How do Update Sets and the Application Repository actually fit together in practice?
options: Update Sets are only used for data records, never configuration
Update Sets track changes day to day as development happens; the Application Repository publishes checkpoint versions at meaningful milestones on top of that work
They are mutually exclusive — a team must choose only one and never use the other
The Application Repository replaces the need for any instance to ever have Production data
questions.explain: Both coexist: Update Sets handle ongoing change promotion, while the Application Repository creates clean, nameable checkpoints at milestones.
